content: The study conducted in the Allahabad district of India, as part of the ChlamIndia study, examined the infections and behavioral determinants influencing sexual and reproductive health. This research was published in Microorganisms in 2019 (Volume 7, Issue 11, Article 1244). Tibaldi and colleagues investigated the presence of vaginal and endocervical microorganisms in both symptomatic and asymptomatic non-pregnant females, identifying associated risk factors and rates of occurrence. Their findings were published in Clinical Microbiology and Infection in 2009 (Volume 15, Issue 7, Pages 670-679). Wand and collaborators assessed the population-attributable risk for chlamydia infections among young international travelers (commonly referred to as backpackers) and residents in Australia. This cohort study was published in BMJ Open in 2011 (Volume 1, Issue 1, Article e000004). Yeung and colleagues conducted a cross-sectional survey to determine the prevalence of chlamydia among young individuals attending rural and regional primary care services in Australia. Their findings were published in the Medical Journal of Australia in 2014 (Volume 200, Issue 3, Pages 170-175). Zimba and collaborators explored the etiology of sexually transmitted infections in Maputo, Mozambique. Their research was published in the Journal of Infection in Developing Countries in 2011 (Volume 5, Issue 1, Pages 41-47).
